segment_performance.highlight: Gross Order Value (GOV) reached ₹4,923 Cr (+130% YoY); store-level contribution margins expanded as dark stores reached 639.
GOV grew 27% YoY to ₹9,264 Cr; adjusted EBITDA margin as % of GOV improved to 3.3% led by platform fee optimization.
Value-added farm-to-kitchen sourcing for 45,000+ restaurant partners with narrowing EBITDA losses.
Ticketing and dining-out experiences being consolidated into the dedicated District lifestyle application.

simple_pointers: **Hyper-Growth in Consolidated Revenue:** Revenue jumped **+74.02% YoY** to **₹4,206 Cr**, driven by explosive 130% YoY expansion in Blinkit quick-commerce GOV.
**Sustained Profitability Trajectory:** Net Profit (PAT) leaped to **₹253 Cr** (compared to ₹20 Cr in the year-ago quarter), demonstrating robust platform network effects.
**Blinkit Crosses Adjusted EBITDA Breakeven:** Quick-commerce achieved milestone positive adjusted EBITDA (+₹32 Cr), dispelling doubts over unit economics.
**Aggressive Dark Store Expansion:** Dark store network expanded to 639 locations with management raising the target to 1,000 dark stores by end-FY27.
**Substantial Net Cash Balance:** Cash balance stands at ₹12,250 Cr, fully funding expansion without debt or dilutive equity issuances.

strengths: Duopoly market leadership in food delivery and #1 market share in Indian quick-commerce (Blinkit).
Immense network effects with 20M+ monthly transacting customers and gold loyalty memberships.
Cash-rich balance sheet (>₹12,000 Cr liquid cash) enabling aggressive 10-minute delivery infrastructure buildout.
weaknesses: Hyperpure and Going-Out segments still generating operational EBITDA losses.
High gig-worker delivery partner attrition requiring recurring driver incentive spends.
opportunities: Expansion into non-grocery quick-commerce categories (electronics, apparel, beauty, festival merchandise).
Higher high-margin in-app advertising revenues from FMCG and consumer tech brands.
threats: Intensified quick-commerce competition from Swiggy Instamart, Zepto, and Tata BigBasket.
Potential gig-economy labor regulations, minimum wage mandates, and rider social security legislation.
